Many people really don't understand how complex Russia as a nation is. That it's not one nation of people but a country with many ethnic groups and cultures in it. I think the easies way for a newbie to get an understanding of it is by looking at the way Russia is organised. If nothing else it shows how much like the USA Russia really is in the way that "states have a lot of autonomy" while the federal government controls more holistic matters. And by looking at the federal subjects it also highlights the existence of different ethnic groups within the country.

Russia is divide into 49 Oblast (provinces), 22 republics, 9 krais (territories), 4 autonomous okurgs (autonomous districts), 1 autonomous oblast and 3 federal cities. And these all exist for different reasons and follow specific characteristic (but as with everything in Russia nothing is exact).

Oblasts are quite similar to US states but nor really. They have a governor and their own parliament (legislator)

Republics are very much like US states. They have their own constitution, are autonomous to a very big extent and have a head of the republic that's very much similar to a US Governor. And these are where the different ethnic groups come in. Republics tend to roughly be areas for specific ethnic groups (of course any Russian can go there etc.). They also tend to have a separate official language side by side with Russian. These control basically everything themselves except for foreign policy just like US states.

Krais are basically what the US used to have but called them Frontiers. Areas under federal control, usually very sparsely populated and so fort. But of course as it's Russia they're also autonomous and the extent they are autonomous I have no idea.

Autonomous Oblast only one of them exists and it is (surprising to many) a Jewish Oblast. It's official name is Jewish Autonomous Oblast. It's a remnant of transformation Soviet organisation. When all other former oblasts were elevated to Republics in the 90s this oblast remained an oblast for some reason. I don't know why.

Federal Cities are like their own regions within another federal district. As an example St. Petersburg which is a Federal City located in Leningrad Oblast. To my understanding they're very much autonomous from the rest of the region. But how much etc. I don't know.

Russia is organised quite much like the US. Only difference is that it has 3 Washington D.C's instead of one and the US has now made states of all the territory it has on the mainland. But not long ago it was still very much like Russia is today in its set up.

So as you see it's organised chaos and there are different ethnic groups, different religious groups etc etc. that are all held together by this loose umbrella concept that's Russia.
